entries.name: Personal health record and portal exports
entries.one_line: A person's own consolidated medical record as they hold it: patient-portal exports, after-visit summaries, and records-request packets.

schema.example: self
schema.why: Whose record this is, read from a labeled patient-identity field. §3.8: 'The system must separate roles that happen to contain the same entity type.' A caregiver's corpus contains records about several people and the holder is not the subject. §3.5: 'Deterministic extractors create direct facts when the information comes from a reliable, explicit source, such as a content hash, EXIF timestamp, a document title, or a labeled form field.'

schema.example: a named patient-portal or EHR system
schema.why: The producing system, read from the export's own manifest or producer metadata rather than from its prose. §3.5: 'Deterministic extractors create direct facts when the information comes from a reliable, explicit source, such as a content hash, EXIF timestamp, a document title, or a labeled form field.'

schema.example: the health system that holds the record
schema.why: Organisation role, distinct from the treating clinician. §3.8: 'The system must separate roles that happen to contain the same entity type.'

schema.example: the export or summary date
schema.why: A labeled date field only; no fuzzy parsing. §3.10: 'The product must not use fuzzy date parsing'

schema.example: after-visit summary
schema.why: Confirmed by the document-structure rule below, not by the filename. §3.13: 'A validated fact was found by a deterministic rule and passed contextual checks, such as a course-code pattern appearing beside “lecture,” “syllabus,” or “semester.”'

deterministic: a patient-portal or EHR export manifest naming the producing system, co-occurring with a labeled patient-identity field and a labeled export or record date in the same file
an after-visit-summary document structure in which a labeled encounter date, a named facility and a labeled patient identity all appear together in the header block
needs_llm: a photographed or scanned paper record whose only signal is prose
a records-request letter that names no facility and carries no patient-identity field
a personal note summarising one's own history, written as free prose
never_alone: a folder named Health, Medical, or Records
a bare person name
a bare date
the word 'patient' occurring in prose
a medical-sounding filename token such as 'chart', 'records', or 'visit'

grouping_reasons: one records-request packet from one facility
one export session from one portal
one subject person's record set

template.why: §5.5: 'For document and record domains, project, function, or subject usually comes before time because putting year first scatters related work across calendar folders.' Facility gives the context needed to read a record type. §5.5: 'a parent dimension should provide the context required to understand the child' `subject person` is optional and must be dropped when it would produce a single child. §5.9: 'It should warn when a level produces only one child'

collides_with.signal: identical vocabulary; the discriminator is holder role, not content. A patient's own portal export names one subject; a clinician's chart set names many, and carries practice-management or EHR-authoring provenance rather than portal-export provenance.
collides_with.design_cite: §3.8: 'The system must separate roles that happen to contain the same entity type.'

collides_with.signal: a portal export bundles lab results inside itself; the bundle is the record, the individual result is the lab-result domain. Extracting both is correct — one file may hold facts from more than one domain.
both carry a labeled person identity; only the health record carries a facility and a clinical document type.
collides_with.design_cite: §3.8: 'The system must separate roles that happen to contain the same entity type.'

entries.sensitivity_why: A person's own medical record — 'potentially sensitive', which is §2.9's own phrase and the whole of what this field asserts. No handling class is set here; classification is P7's (§8.4).
entries.open_question: Should a person's own records and a dependant's records share one branch with `subject person` as the first dimension, or should each subject person get their own top-level branch? For a single-person corpus `subject person` produces exactly the one-child level §5.9 tells the product to warn about; for a caregiver it is the only sane first split. This is a default folder shape for someone's real family and is Joseph's call, not the catalogue's.

Does the exception extend to them? Joseph's call; the catalogue follows the stated default until he says otherwise.

a species or breed name
the words 'pet', 'dog', 'cat' or 'vet' in a filename

grouping_reasons: one animal's record set
one travel requirement and the documents assembled for it

template.why: §5.5: 'For document and record domains, project, function, or subject usually comes before time because putting year first scatters related work across calendar folders.' The animal is the only sensible first dimension in a household with more than one. §5.5: 'a parent dimension should provide the context required to understand the child'

collides_with.signal: the same records held by the other party; the owner holds one animal's set, the clinic holds many.
an animal vaccination certificate and a human one are the same document shape, and a household corpus contains both.
animal travel certificates are assembled for a specific trip and are purpose-coherent with it.
collides_with.design_cite: §3.9: 'Topic answers what a file is about, while purpose answers what the file was for.'

entries.sensitivity_why: Records naming an owner, their address, and their animals — 'potentially sensitive', which is §2.9's own phrase and the whole of what this field asserts. No handling class is set here; classification is P7's (§8.4).
